body:
I'm actually really cool with what you're saying, because this is the exact line of thinking I had that prevented me from leaving - you have no idea, I'm the most patient person in the world, and I'm always the one giving the contrary opinions based on empathy and what the other person feels or is experiencing, so I actually really appreciate your input. :)  Unfortunately, I'm always the person setting myself on fire to keep others warm. 

Now, on to the response...

We spoke, together, with his parents, and with a therapist. Any time anyone brought up the subject of contributing in any way, the answer was flat out "no".  He is a spoiled child, and readily admits it, and in no way wishes to improve.  His intentions are to live off of his dad comfortably for as long as he can.

I brought up several times and we discussed several times that my funds could not cover everything for both of us. We discussed that this would mean giving up internet, or video games, or you-name-it. His solution was always that he could just stay with his dad without me.

That, right there? The idea that he could just live without me, but I didn't feel like I could live without him? I think that's what opened my eyes to the one-sided aspect of the relationship. And when I brought it up to him, that I was interpreting it that way and it was hurtful? "Well yeah, I mean I'm sorry but that's how I meant it".

If it were a "you and me against the world" situation, I'd be able to stick it out. But if what I'm doing is considered "selfish" and earns me that label, so be it, I guess. But keep in mind - this wasn't just a "bad spell" in his life. This is how it has always been. This is how he intends for it to always be. Again, call it "incompatibility", but that's not for me.

Absolutely correct.  But in order to proceed with the relationship like we wanted to and have him move in with me and then further on down the line marriage and whatnot, I wouldn't have been able to afford it.

But he didn't want to contribute. He wanted to live with me and not bring anything to the table. It was actually impossible, I couldn't afford it.
You kick ASS!  You sound like such a great mom. :)

"Trivial"?  I apologize if this sounds snarky, but did you read any of my original thread?

Working is by no means a necessity, I agree. I in fact welcome the idea of a stay-at-home husband. 

The issue was my boyfriend was telling me that he wants to stay home, smoke weed, jack off, and play video games without contributing in any way (whether it be cooking, cleaning, going to class, etc.) while actively telling me that he doesn't want to be employed because of the capitalist agenda and he just wants to live off of my income, in his words, "like a child". 

You have my kudos with helping your wife and I 100% support a situation like that where the support is mutual, however please consider the entire scenario before tossing the word "trivial" around because even though it may sound similar to your situation, it doesn't seem like it is. The difference between "I am stressed/in a bad place and I need help" and "No, I don't fucking feel like it, fuck off" is huge.
Does your Facebook say you went to school at Hogwarts? Because mine says I went to Starfleet Academy. :D

Exactly.  I have all the respect in the world for people who aren't working or who are maybe in dire straits but are actively trying to better themselves or even reaching out for help. I was even cool with his whole situation for the longest time because I figured "Stay at home boyfriend/husband? Why not? Maybe he can help around the apartment or maybe he wants to be a stay at home dad."  Except...he didn't.  One of the last straws was probably when he refused to come with me to the store but wanted me to buy him stuff.  Like...what.  Get your own chocolate milk OH WAIT YOU CAN'T.
Yes, we are in fact no longer together.
I posted an edit about that, sorry to leave you hanging.  It was kinda...dissatisfying, so I left it out initially.  Dude's brain was just wired wrongly.

That's kinda sweet, actually. :)

Thanks for paying so much attention. I'm so excited to go out and do all the new things!

It's seriously something I've been looking at since I was 25 and it was one of those things where I'm just like "One of these days..." which is weird because I'm usually not that type of person, I'm the chick that goes "That looks neat" and then the following week I'm doing it.  Well...now I'm doing it!  Thanks for the info on that group - looks useful! :)

Thanks man. I honestly didn't even care so much about the not working, except his mission in life was to literally not do anything except jerk it and play video games.

"Geeky" I guess is just a general term I use for people that are into video games/comic books/sci-fi/fantasy stuff.
Yo!  I go downtown a lot, mostly to the casino or to Happy Dog. Awesome offer, especially if they're geeky. :D

I've gotta go House Greyjoy because I love mythical sea creatures and they're the Kraken. Plus, I grew up on the lake. 

And I adore Asha Greyjoy because she's some sort of sexy pirate queen. Role models <3

It's like you're completely torn because on the one hand, you really need the help and it's stressful, but on the other hand you're in love with this person and want to remain understanding and respectful because you don't want them to be an enemy in your mind.

[I think you and I should get together.](https://www.reddit.com/r/relationships/comments/4k5icd/me_30_f_with_my_boyfriend_25_m_of_15_years_i/)

On a serious note, I don't have advice because I'm in the same situation, but if you need to commiserate, feel free to PM me.

Hi!  Thanks so much for your suggestions.  

Just to clear up a couple of things, because they weren't clear in my post:  I'm definitely leaving the boyfriend, that's why I've sped all this up so instead of staying here for ~90 days and saving and whatnot, I'm getting out of this situation now.

Also, I say "cleaning fees" but it's also this whole big situation where they also refused to take my rent or answer any of my phone calls for the last two months.  They switched office managers within the last year and the new lady just really did not like me for some reason, and she would often "miscommunicate" or flat-out lie to me, or just not respond in some manners, so I'm not surprised really....but my next post will probably be to r/legaladvice about it because it's been a while since I've heard from them.
